intent: Trigger one action on the attachment, such as removing or downloading it, as a small ghost button.
typical_uses: An icon-only remove or download button on an attached file

dont_use_when.situation: An action that does not act on an attachment
Opening or previewing the whole attachment by clicking the card

invariants.text: AttachmentAction renders Button's `ghost` variant when `variant` is not given or is null.
The button is squared as icon-only only when the icon is passed through `icon` with no children (Button's `data-icon-only`); it then has no accessible name of its own and needs an `aria-label`.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave an icon-only action without an `aria-label`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Name the action and its target, such as aria-label="Remove report.pdf"

a11y.by: attachment.test.tsx asserts that an AttachmentAction with aria-label="Remove" is found by role "button" with the accessible name "Remove"

icon.states: icon is a React node, not a value
icon.because: `ReactNode` is a union of an element, a string, a number, a fragment, `false` and more - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is Button's icon slot, which sizes the icon, hides it while `loading` and marks it `aria-hidden`.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the button's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through button.module.css and attachment.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: The icon passed as children
bad.why: Children are Button's label: the icon lands in the label span and the button is not squared as icon-only, since Button sets `data-icon-only` only for an `icon` with no children. Pass it through `icon`.

icon.description: Partially typed: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. icon is a React node, not a value. `ReactNode` is a union of an element, a string, a number, a fragment, `false` and more - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is Button's icon slot, which sizes the icon, hides it while `loading` and marks it `aria-hidden`.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ButtonState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ButtonState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the button's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through button.module.css and attachment.module.css, not through this.
